notices.summary: Use the completion checklist, verify outside-department credit approval, and check degree requirements with ECE each semester.
notices.context: 수료 means completing the program’s coursework requirements; it is different from receiving a degree. A handbook or the university simulator alone does not establish that ECE has approved your individual credits or research record.
notices.applicability: Relevant if you are in an ECE graduate program and need to check completion, qualifying-exam credits or research-output recognition. Your individual eligibility remains conditional on ECE’s assessment; the notice does not separately resolve international or exchange cases.

steps: Use the attached self-check spreadsheet and graduate handbook to check your coursework; these files still need to be read.

For outside-department credits, obtain advisor approval and follow linked notice 56284. Unrelated/general-education courses are excluded; outside-department recognition is capped at half the required completion credits, and ECE graduate credits excluding Thesis Research must exceed outside-department plus undergraduate credits.

If you already submitted an outside-department credit-approval application, complete the linked Google Form so the office can cross-check it: https://forms.gle/zpizs3KyqNtxcmgh7 . The form does not replace the approval application.
For qualifying-exam eligibility, count at least six ECE graduate credits, excluding Thesis Research, S/U courses, the specified modular seminars and credits carried across programs.
Recheck the current semester’s academic notices and ask the graduate office about ambiguous course or research-output recognition.
exceptions: ECE-administered course codes starting 430 or M2608 count as major courses; some AI-semiconductor interdisciplinary courses may also qualify, but require an office inquiry.
A course with a 430 prefix can still be excluded from the qualifying-exam six-credit requirement if it is a modular seminar.
PhD/integrated research-output recognition is subject to department rules and individual assessment. Use the current semester’s rule notice rather than treating this FAQ as an unconditional approval.

The later credit-approval notice 58023 gives a different cap formula for entrants from 2021: (required completion credits minus Thesis Research credits) × 1/2. Check that cohort-specific rule rather than relying on this FAQ’s general half-credit wording.

notices.title: Use the correct research-output rules for your thesis-review semester
notices.summary: From Fall 2026, a master’s journal submission alone no longer counts. Acceptance/publication evidence must exist by the result-document deadline.
notices.context: A paper being submitted, accepted and published are different statuses. The notice’s rule changes are tied to the thesis-review semester, rather than simply your year of admission. This March rule notice must also be checked against any later rule update linked by the current semester’s review notice.
notices.applicability: Only if you are an ECE graduate student checking the research-output component of degree conferral. Spring 2026 review candidates use the earlier section; Fall 2026 onward candidates use the revised section, subject to current department updates. Individual recognition is not guaranteed.
eligibility_quotes: 대학원 전체 대상(석사, 박사, 석박통합 과정)
2026년 9월부터(2026학년도 2학기 심사대상자부터) 적용
steps: Identify your thesis-review semester before using either rule set. Recheck the current semester’s review notice and any newer rule notice.

For the revised master’s rule, prepare at least one domestic/international conference or journal paper that is published or accepted. You must be first author excluding your advisor, and the advisor must be a coauthor. Co-first authorship is not accepted for master’s students.

For the revised PhD/integrated rule, meet BOTH conditions: at least one internationally recognized SCI(E)-level journal paper, AND at least one international conference paper, domestic journal paper, or registered international patent. The first two routes require publication or acceptance. The advisor/coauthor and first-author conditions apply.
Obtain publication or acceptance evidence that can be issued before the thesis-review result-document deadline. Get that exact deadline from the current semester’s notice; none is dated here.
Ask the graduate office to decide any ambiguous output, authorship or recognition case. Other degree requirements remain in force.
exceptions: For review through Spring 2026, the earlier master’s section permits journal-submission proof by reference to that semester’s review guidance. This does not carry into Fall 2026.
A registered international patent is an alternative only for the second PhD/integrated condition; it does not replace the first journal condition.
The department warns that the new rule may be edited and individual recognition depends on its final assessment. This brief does not import a later rule without reading it.
notices.forms_note: No attachment is listed on this saved page. Linked rules on recognized conferences and co-first authorship require separate reading.

terms.en: Submission to a journal; it is not acceptance.
Acceptance for publication, supported by evidence such as an acceptance email.
The research output that the department agrees to count toward a degree requirement.

consequence.text: The notice explicitly says journal-submission evidence is not recognized for Fall 2026 review candidates onward. It does not give a separate penalty.

masters.text: From Fall 2026: at least one conference/journal paper published or accepted; you are first author excluding the advisor, and the advisor is a coauthor. Submission alone and co-first authorship are excluded for master’s. Abstract-only conferences require peer review and signed confirmation. Get evidence before the result-paper deadline.

masters.title: Finish review, result papers and BOTH final submissions
masters.text: Online application and paper documents, fee, manuscript/presentation, result papers, library PDF and office approval documents are separate stages. Fall results: master’s 14 December 2026 at 17:00. Office final papers close 22 January 2027 at 17:00, earlier than the library’s 1 February 23:59 cutoff.

phd.title: Check completion credits and recognition
phd.text: Use ECE’s self-check and handbook rather than assuming the university simulator includes departmental rules. Check cohort-dependent outside-department credit approval and the graduate-program cap on undergraduate credits.

phd.title: Pass the qualifying exam, then arrange preliminary review
phd.text: Verify major and language passes. PhD preliminary review must finish by the semester before initial/final thesis review. The current preliminary-review notice targets August 2027 degrees; individual stage and timing still need checking.

phd.title: Meet BOTH PhD research-output conditions
phd.text: An SCI(E)-level journal publication/acceptance AND an international conference paper, domestic journal paper or registered international patent are required under the current rule. First-author/advisor-coauthor conditions and any cohort exceptions need checking. Abstract-only output requires peer review and signed confirmation.

phd.title: Complete initial/final review and final thesis deposit
phd.text: Prepare the five-member review process and degree-specific result documents. Fall PhD results: 21 December 2026 at 17:00. Office final papers close 22 January 2027 at 17:00; library PDF closes 1 February 23:59. Contact ECE BEFORE any deadline if an exception is needed.

integrated.title: Verify integrated-program coursework and status
integrated.text: Use ECE’s self-check, handbook and cohort-specific approval rules. Do not substitute the master’s completion requirements. Coursework completion and degree conferral are different statuses.

integrated.title: Check the integrated qualifying-exam route
integrated.text: Verify both major and language results and current registration rules. The historical Spring 2026 example requires integrated students to sit in their third registered semester; that example does not establish a later exam’s dates or your overall eligibility.

integrated.title: Follow PhD preliminary-review and output requirements
integrated.text: Preliminary review precedes initial/final review by at least a semester. The current publication notice places integrated students under the two-part PhD output requirement; check authorship, proof timing and abstract-only conference confirmation.

integrated.title: Complete review and the correct thesis-course confirmations
integrated.text: If taking two Thesis Research sections, obtain prior permission and one confirmation per professor. Later thesis review and final deposit have separate degree-specific documents and dates. Use the current notice rather than old semester examples.

undergraduate.title: Check your cohort’s curriculum and registered course codes
undergraduate.text: Course classification, prerequisites and offering semesters can depend on entry cohort. Cross-listed codes are not interchangeable: another major’s code can count as general elective, and a retake uses the original code. The spring guide is a historical example, not a complete current graduation audit.

undergraduate.title: Complete the graduation project’s actual milestones
undergraduate.text: For the Fall 2026 project: poster PDF 9 November at 23:59, advisor review by 16 November, panel setup 19 November and presentation 20 November. For Spring 2027 preparation, follow the separate preference/interview/allocation rounds.

undergraduate.title: Get the thesis signed even if you graduate later
undergraduate.text: Writing/signing the project thesis and handing it in are separate requirements. Non-graduating students still complete the signature this project semester and keep the approved thesis. Prior advisor permission is required for the stated signature extension.

undergraduate.title: Submit under the correct graduation application
undergraduate.text: February 2027 ECE primary/double-major graduation applicants submit the prescribed signed thesis in December by 21 December. The stated delayed hand-in requires its confirmation by the normal deadline, then thesis delivery by 28 December. Other graduation requirements still need office checking.
